canonical_name: Simons minimal-submanifold rigidity theorem family (repository title: 辛格定理)
source_claim_verbatim_translation: A rigidity theorem for minimal surfaces.
canonical_statement: Provisional theorem-family boundary: a source-pinned rigidity or pinching theorem for minimal surfaces or minimal submanifolds associated by repository metadata with James Simons's 1968 work. The repository does not determine whether the root is the Simons identity, a pointwise/integral inequality, a strict pinching gap theorem, or an equality classification.
statement_selection: open: resolve the Singer/Simons title conflict and select an exact primary-source theorem
domain_and_universes: Open: a smooth minimal immersion or minimal submanifold in a selected Riemannian ambient manifold, probably a sphere for a pinching result; manifold universes, scalar field, dimension, codimension, regularity, connectedness, completeness, compactness, and boundary assumptions are not fixed by repository metadata.
quantifiers: minimal immersion or minimal submanifold M in an ambient Riemannian manifold N
dimensions and codimension required by the selected source theorem
points, frames, or integrated domain required by the selected identity or inequality
hypotheses: minimality in the exact source sense
ambient curvature and normalization assumptions from the selected theorem
compactness, connectedness, orientability, completeness, or boundary hypotheses only when source-required
the exact pointwise or integral pinching bound if a rigidity branch is selected
conclusion: The exact identity, inequality, total-geodesy conclusion, or extremal classification stated by the selected primary source.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: James Simons versus I. M. Singer and whether the Chinese title is a transliteration error
surface dimension two versus an arbitrary-dimensional minimal submanifold
Euclidean, spherical, or general Riemannian ambient space and its curvature normalization
Simons differential identity versus its integrated inequality or a derived pinching theorem
strict pinching rigidity versus threshold equality and classification
hypersurface versus higher codimension, including the norm and threshold constants
which conclusions belong to Simons 1968 and which require later classification papers
